label: L-02
title: UniswapHelper add-liquidity guard is existence-only, so an honest user can become first LP of the empty canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair and permanently brick both the cutover core (step 2) and UniPoolerCutoverEscrow (PairNotEmpty); story-109's stated safety rationale is not achieved

instances.note: runbook premise 'pair does not exist until Stage 4'

rootCause: _requirePair() reverts only when getPair == 0, not when reserves are (0,0); story 109/111 treat 'pair does not exist' as the safety boundary, but createPair is permissionless and cutover step 1 creates the pair in its own tx before step 6 seeds it.
description: The helper gates liquidity on the canonical pair EXISTING, not on it having reserves. Story 111 deploys the helper BEFORE the cutover. The pair exists from cutover step 1 onward, and earlier if anyone calls the permissionless factory.createPair. Any addLiquidity through the helper while the pair is still empty makes that caller the first LP and gives the pair non-zero reserves. That permanently fails core step 2 (L339/344) and the escrow's PairNotEmpty, and UniPoolerV2's canonical-pair constructor check means no alternative pair can be used. The deploy script's NatSpec (DeployUniswapHelperMainnet.s.sol L43-46) presents 'pair does not exist' as the safety boundary. That boundary does not cover the step-1..step-6 window or a pre-created pair.

attackPath: 1. UniswapHelper is deployed via uniswap-helper:broadcast (story 111) before Stage 4
2. The canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair comes to exist: cutover step 1 in its own tx, or anyone calling permissionless factory.createPair
3. An honest user (or a UI exposing the add form once getPair resolves) calls addLiquiditySUSDS/USDS; _requirePair only checks existence
4. Pair reserves become non-zero permanently; core step 2 reverts 'pair reserves not empty', escrow reverts PairNotEmpty (0x247b45ec)
failureScenario.attackVector: Unlike the ledgered attacker poisoning, this can be triggered by an honest user or a UI build that exposes the add-liquidity form once the pair address resolves. The helper resolves it live via getPair, independent of the PhusdSusdsPair address-book key.
failureScenario.likelihood: low-medium - requires the pair to exist before seeding and a user/UI to add liquidity in that window; the adversarial version already exists without the helper
failureScenario.assumptions: Helper deployed before cutover (story 111 permits this); pair created before seeding
failureScenario.externalRequirements: A third party (honest or not) adds liquidity to the empty pair

impact: Permanently bricks the current seeding contracts (core step 2 and escrow PairNotEmpty); finishing needs new re-price-then-mint code, with the recovery exit as the backstop. MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY lock means reserves can never return to 0; UniPoolerV2 canonical-pair constructor forbids an alternative pair (the pair itself stays usable); first LP sets the price. Liveness, no direct theft.
assetImpact: None stolen; permanently bricks the current seeding contracts (core step 2 and escrow PairNotEmpty) once any non-zero first mint occurs (MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY lock); finishing needs new re-price-then-mint code, with the recovery exit as the backstop.

exactReverts: core step 2: 'UniPoolerCutoverCore: pair reserves not empty'

recommendation: Revert in the helper's add paths when either reserve is 0 (EmptyPair) so the helper can never be the first LP. Correct runbook/story-111 wording: the pair may exist before Stage 4.

classification.justification: Fork-proven (test_CODE005_helperFirstLPBricksCoreStep2AndEscrow), and Law 1 overrides story 109: the story's stated safety rationale (helper cannot seed before the cutover) is not achieved, because existence is not emptiness. It is not Medium because (a) no asset is at risk and the protocol's live functions (index-4 minting, which does not touch Balancer) are unaffected; (b) the incremental risk over the already-accepted adversarial brick (ledger 9a694ae01fe1 open Low; ycn L-26 wont-fix, owner: 'it should just panic and then I'll have to figure out what to do') is a new honest trigger, not a new outcome; (c) the brick is of a specific seeding design, not of the protocol: the owner can still seed the poisoned pair by re-pricing a dust-sized first position and minting into it (plan L414 sketches exactly this recovery), at the cost of new code; (d) L-26's re-weigh condition ('a hard deadline would expose value') is only partly met: the deadline exists, but value is not exposed, because a proportional recovery exit stays open after 30 Nov (plan L22/L38). The fix is a one-line reserve check in the helper, and it must land before story 111 broadcasts. Re-raise disclosure: this is a distinct contract and trigger from ycn L-26 b2a29359fde5 (wont-fix 2026-10-07), whose quoted triage reason is carried in the finding.

reweighTrigger: Raise to Medium if the protocol UI exposes the helper's add-liquidity form before Stage 4, or if story 103 keeps step 1 (createPair) in a separate tx from the seed with the helper live; disclose ycn L-26 b2a29359fde5 wont-fix on any re-weigh.

storyFaithfulness.summary: Letter of story 109 satisfied (blocks pair creation through the helper); its stated purpose (prevent seeding before 103's cutover) is not. Law 1 overrides: the spec ships an honest-user path to the 9a694ae01fe1 brick.

wontFixDisclosure.quotedTriageReason: Owner triage 2026-10-07: wont-fix. Owner: "I guess, it should just panic and then I'll have to figure out what to do if there is a pair. I think it's safe to mark as won't fix." Basis: the escrow's strict empty-pair gate is fail-loud by design — a synced donation or dust first-mint only reverts exitAndSeed; no value moves and abort() fully restores the old pooler (fork-proven run-22). Recovery from a poisoned pair is an attended, manual operator decision ... Re-weigh if a hard deadline would expose value, or if no replacement seeder is permissible under the story-052 tax constraint.
wontFixDisclosure.whyNotSameDefect: L-26 judged the ESCROW's fail-loud gate against an ADVERSARIAL 1-wei grief. DEDUP-002 is a defect in a different, newer first-party contract (UniswapHelper, story 109) that offers the first-LP path to honest users through the protocol's own UI surface; the owner's 'just panic' acceptance does not address the protocol itself shipping the trigger, and its stated re-weigh condition (hard deadline) now holds.

Not Medium: no asset at risk and live protocol functions unaffected; the adversarial-trigger outcome is already accepted (9a694ae01fe1 open Low; ycn L-26 b2a29359fde5 wont-fix 2026-10-07); the brick hits one seeding design, not the protocol (dust first position can be re-priced and minted into with new code, plan L414); L-26 re-weigh condition only partly met (deadline exists, value not exposed because the recovery exit stays open).
Re-raises an owner wont-fix (ycn L-26) on a new contract and trigger; the human may wish to re-weigh L-26 given the 30 Oct / 30 Nov deadlines.
severityRaiseTrigger: Raise to Medium if the protocol UI exposes the helper add-liquidity form before Stage 4, or if story 103 keeps step 1 (createPair) in a separate tx from the seed while the helper is live; disclose ycn L-26 b2a29359fde5 wont-fix on any re-weigh.
wontFixDisclosureText: DISCLOSURE: this finding re-raises yield-claim-nft L-26 b2a29359fde5, which the owner triaged wont-fix on 2026-10-07. Quoted triageReason: "I guess, it should just panic and then I'll have to figure out what to do if there is a pair. I think it's safe to mark as won't fix." ... "Re-weigh if a hard deadline would expose value, or if no replacement seeder is permissible under the story-052 tax constraint." It is kept rather than suppressed because it is a different contract (UniswapHelper, story 109, auto-complete), a different root cause (existence-only guard), a different trigger (honest user through a protocol-shipped helper, vs an adversarial 1-wei grief), and a different fix location (the helper, not the escrow). L-26 re-weigh condition now partly holds: BalancerWinddownPlan.md L7 sets withdrawals-only from 30 Oct 2026 and V3 Vault paused 30 Nov 2026.
fixDeadline: One-line reserve check in the helper before story 111 broadcasts.
rePriceAnalysis: Severity-auditor re-price math (review/severity-audit.md): an honest 1e18 sUSDS / 1e18 phUSD first LP overprices phUSD by about 21% versus the live fair ratio (~0.82 sUSDS per phUSD); a few-cent arbitrage swap re-prices the ~$2 pool (the protocol can be the arbitrageur); minting in afterwards is pro-rata, so protocol dilution is about $2 against ~$41k. A larger mispriced first LP makes the re-price a gain to the protocol, not a loss. No protocol asset at risk.
reviewEdits: 2026-10-13 final review: replaced "permanently bricks the cutover design" wording with the seeding-contracts wording (severity-audit: overstatement); added the severity auditor re-price math. Severity unchanged (Low).
